# t19.1 — Shared Android lint blockers and serialized Gradle gate

## Summary

Resolved the 67 `LocalContextGetResourceValueCall` lint errors in `CycleScreen.kt` and `WorkoutFeatureScreen.kt` without disabling lint rules. A clean, single-worker Gradle test/build/package gate passed. No backend/API or HTTPS-policy source was changed.

## Changes

- Replaced Compose UI resource reads through `LocalContext.current.getString()` with Compose `stringResource`.
- Resolved cycle validation and persistence-error messages during composition before event/coroutine callbacks use them.
- Made workout state/error message helpers composable, and resolved the heart-rate accessibility description before entering the non-composable semantics lambda.
- Did not add lint suppressions, change lint configuration, change target SDK/dependencies, or modify the typed API client. Its production HTTPS requirement remains in place; cleartext continues to require the explicit loopback-debug opt-in.

## Test Results

- Command: `.\gradlew.bat clean test build assembleDebugAndroidTest --no-daemon --no-parallel --max-workers=1` (from `D:\Proyectos\Nutri\android`, with JDK 17.0.16 and Android SDK 36 activated in the same PowerShell process).
- Gradle exit code: `0`; result: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` (2m 20s; 137 actionable tasks).
- JVM tests: **58 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (13 XML reports).
- Build/lint: debug and release builds passed; `:app:lintDebug`, `:app:lint`, and `:app:check` passed. Fresh lint report: **0 errors, 22 warnings, 1 hint**. The remaining warnings/hint were not suppressed or reclassified.
- Android instrumentation: test sources compiled and the APK was assembled. Instrumented tests were **not run**: `adb devices -l` showed no devices and `emulator -accel-check` exited `6` because the Android Emulator hypervisor driver is unavailable.
- HTTPS boundary: `NutriaApiClient.kt` still accepts HTTPS, or HTTP only when the explicit local-debug option is enabled and the URL host is loopback.

## Remaining Validation Boundary

This closes the shared lint/build blocker only. It does not establish feature parity, real-device behavior, Health Connect behavior, BLE-band behavior, or instrumentation runtime success. Those validations remain outstanding.
